mainTopic: Closing life-advice teachings (identifying a רבי, eating modestly), then the start of the סדר: the בית שמאי / בית הלל dispute over the order of the blessings on the first cup.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a string of practical life-advice sayings. The גמרא notes that two names refer to the same Sage. Then רבי יהודה בר אילעי advises eating simply and investing in one's home, and עולא adds a proverb from ארץ ישראל with the same message. A new משנה then begins the סדר: once the first cup is poured, בית שמאי say to bless the day (קידוש) first, while בית הלל say to bless the wine first. The גמרא brings a ברייתא giving two reasons for each side, ending with the ruling that the הלכה follows בית הלל. It explains why בית הלל added a second reason, and why the ruling had to be stated at all when a בת קול had already favored בית הלל. Finally, the next משנה describes the first dipping in חזרת and the foods placed before the leader: מצה, חזרת, חרוסת, two cooked dishes, and, when the בית המקדש stood, the קרבן פסח itself. On חרוסת, the תנא קמא and רבי אליעזר בן צדוק disagree about whether eating it is a מצוה.

steps.title: Two names, one Sage
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא states that רבי יצחק בן אחא, who appears in הלכה, is the same person as רבי יצחק בן פנחס, who appears in אגדה, and gives a memory aid.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבי יצחק בן אחא who appears in הלכה is the same as the רבי יצחק בן פנחס who appears in אגדה. Your memory aid is the phrase: 'Listen, my brothers and friends.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to clear up a name confusion. It tells us that one Sage is quoted under two different names.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In legal teachings (שמעתא) he is called בן אחא, and in story or homiletic teachings (אגדתא) he is called בן פנחס. The memory phrase links the two: 'שמעו' sounds like 'שמעתא', the word for הלכה, and 'אחיי' sounds like 'אחא'. So the הלכה name is the אחא name.

keyTerms.meaning: A legal teaching or halachic ruling
Non-legal teaching, such as stories, ethics, or homiletics
Your mnemonic, a memory aid

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a הלכה about anything. It is only a note identifying who a Sage is. Do not look for a legal point in it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak ben Acha of the halachic teachings,

phrases.aramaic: הוּא רַבִּי יִצְחָק בֶּן פִּנְחָס דְּאַגָּדְתָּא.
phrases.english: he is Rabbi Yitzchak ben Pinchas of the aggadic teachings.
phrases.notes: Same person, two names, depending on the type of teaching.

phrases.english: And your mnemonic: 'Listen, please, my brothers and friends.'
phrases.notes: שמעו hints to שמעתא (הלכה), and אחיי hints to אחא.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יִצְחָק בֶּן אַחָא דִּשְׁמַעְתָּא, הוּא רַבִּי יִצְחָק בֶּן פִּנְחָס דְּאַגָּדְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens this passage. It is an identification note attached to the preceding run of teachings on the daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יצחק בן אחא (in הלכה) and רבי יצחק בן פנחס (in אגדה) are one and the same Sage.

steps.title: Eat simply, invest in your home
steps.stepSummary: Through a chain of tradition, רבי יהודה בר אילעי advises eating cheap food in comfort instead of luxury food, and spending less on food and more on housing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן, quoting רבי יהודה son of רבי אילעי: Eat an onion and sit in the shade. Do not eat geese and chickens, or your heart will chase after you. Spend less on your food and drink, and add to your house.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings practical financial and lifestyle advice: live modestly with food and put your money into your home.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wordplay בָּצָל / בַּצֵּל (onion / shade) teaches that simple food in a comfortable setting beats fancy food. Expensive meats create a craving for luxury ('your heart will chase you') that you cannot keep paying for. A house is a lasting investment, while food is used up and gone.

keyTerms.meaning: In the name of, quoting
Onion / shade (a play on words)
Chases after you, meaning a craving that keeps pushing you
Your dwelling, your house

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Chana said that Rabbi Yochanan said
in the name of Rabbi Yehuda son of Rabbi Elai:
Eat an onion and sit in the shade,
and do not eat geese and chickens,
lest your heart chase after you.
phrases.notes: You will develop cravings you cannot afford.

phrases.english: Reduce your food and your drink,
and add to your dwelling.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בְּרַבִּי אִילְעַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of practical life-advice teachings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Live modestly with food. Avoid luxury eating that breeds craving, and invest in your home instead.

steps.title: עולא's proverb from ארץ ישראל on luxury eating
steps.stepSummary: עולא reports a popular saying from ארץ ישראל: the one who eats fancy fat tail ends up hiding from creditors, while the one who eats plain vegetables can rest anywhere without worry.
steps.simpleTranslation: When עולא came, he said: They say a proverb in the West (ארץ ישראל): One who eats fat tail hides in the attic. One who eats vegetables lies down on the city's garbage heaps.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא adds a folk proverb from ארץ ישראל that makes the same point as the previous teaching: expensive eating leads to debt and fear.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Again there is wordplay: אַלְיְתָא / עִלִּיתָא (fat tail / attic) and קָקוּלִי / קִיקְלֵי (vegetables / garbage heaps). The luxury eater looks rich, so creditors come after him and he must hide upstairs. The simple eater owes nothing, so he can lie down even in the most public, lowly place and fear no one.

keyTerms.meaning: A proverb, a popular saying
The West, meaning ארץ ישראל (west of Bavel)
Fat tail of a sheep, a delicacy
Hides
The city's garbage heaps

steps.whatToRemember: Both sayings teach the same lesson: luxury eating leads to cravings and debt, while simple living brings security and peace of mind.

phrases.english: When Ulla came, he said:
phrases.notes: He came from ארץ ישראל to Bavel.

phrases.english: They tell a proverb in the West:
One who eats fat tail hides in the attic.
phrases.notes: He hides from creditors who think he is wealthy.

phrases.english: One who eats vegetables lies down on the city's garbage heaps.
phrases.notes: He has no debts, so he fears no one.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא עוּלָּא, אָמַר: מַתְלָא מָתְלִין בְּמַעְרְבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel saying that reinforces step 2's advice about modest eating.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Luxury eating leads to debt and hiding, while simple eating leads to freedom from worry.

steps.title: New משנה: which blessing comes first on the first cup
steps.stepSummary: The משנה begins describing the סדר. Once the first cup is poured, בית שמאי say to bless the day (קידוש) first and then the wine. בית הלל say to bless the wine first and then the day.
steps.simpleTranslation: They poured him the first cup. בית שמאי say: He blesses on the day, and afterward he blesses on the wine. בית הלל say: He blesses on the wine, and afterward he blesses on the day.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts the order of the סדר night with the first of the four cups. It presents a dispute about the order of two blessings: בורא פרי הגפן and the קידוש blessing for the day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree that two blessings are said over the first cup. They argue only about which comes first. 'Blessing on the day' means the קידוש that declares the holiness of יום טוב. The גמרא will explain the reasoning behind each side.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for מתניתין, 'our משנה', marking a new משנה
They poured or mixed (wine was often mixed with water)
The first cup of the four cups at the סדר
Recites the blessing on the day, meaning קידוש
Recites the blessing on wine (בורא פרי הגפן)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think they disagree about whether to make קידוש. Both agree there are two blessings. The only question is their order. Our practice (wine first, then קידוש) follows בית הלל.
steps.whyThisMatters: This dispute sets the order of every קידוש we make on שבת and יום טוב. We follow בית הלל and say הגפן before the blessing of the day.

phrases.english: MISHNA: They poured for him the first cup.

phrases.aramaic: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: מְבָרֵךְ עַל הַיּוֹם,
phrases.english: Beit Shammai say: He blesses over the day,
and afterward he blesses over the wine.

phrases.aramaic: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים: מְבָרֵךְ עַל הַיַּיִן,
phrases.english: And Beit Hillel say: He blesses over the wine,
and afterward he blesses over the day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from aggadic life advice to a new משנה about the סדר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי: קידוש of the day first, then wine. בית הלל: wine first, then קידוש of the day.

steps.title: A ברייתא gives בית שמאי's two reasons for blessing the day first
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא listing the disputes between בית שמאי and בית הלל about the meal. בית שמאי bless the day first because the day is what brings the wine. Also, the day was already holy before the wine arrived.
steps.simpleTranslation: The גמרא: The Sages taught: These are the disputes between בית שמאי and בית הלל about the meal. בית שמאי say: One blesses the day first and then blesses the wine. This is because the day is the reason the wine is brought. Also, the day already became holy while the wine had not yet come.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens its discussion of the משנה by bringing a ברייתא that explains why בית שמאי bless the day (קידוש) before the wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי give two reasons. First, the wine is only on the table because it is שבת or יום טוב, so the day is the main thing. Second, the day became holy at nightfall, before the wine was even brought, so it came first in time and should be blessed first.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The Sages taught.' This introduces a ברייתא, a teaching from the time of the משנה that is not in the משנה itself.
Meal
Causes / is the reason for
The day became holy (at nightfall)

phrases.english: Gemara:
phrases.notes: The start of the גמרא's discussion of the משנה.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:

phrases.aramaic: דְּבָרִים שֶׁבֵּין בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵית הִלֵּל בַּסְּעוּדָה.
phrases.english: These are the matters of dispute between Beis Shammai and Beis Hillel regarding the meal.
Beis Shammai say:
One blesses over the day (kiddush),
and afterward blesses over the wine,
because the day causes the wine to be brought,
phrases.notes: Reason 1: the wine is there only because of שבת or יום טוב.

phrases.english: and the day has already become holy
phrases.notes: Reason 2: the day came first in time.

phrases.english: while the wine has not yet come.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: דְּבָרִים שֶׁבֵּין בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵית הִלֵּל בַּסְּעוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that gives the reasoning behind בית שמאי's position in the משנה (Step 4).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי: bless the day first, because the day causes the wine to be brought and the day was already holy before the wine arrived.

steps.title: בית הלל's two reasons for blessing the wine first
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל bless the wine first, because without wine there would be no קידוש. As a second reason, the wine blessing is said often, and something done often comes first.
steps.simpleTranslation: And בית הלל say: One blesses the wine first and then blesses the day. This is because the wine is what makes it possible to say קידוש. Another reason: the blessing on wine is said often, while the blessing on the day is not said often. When something frequent meets something infrequent, the frequent one comes first.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with בית הלל's side and gives two reasons for blessing the wine first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reason 1 flips בית שמאי's logic: the wine causes the קידוש, since you cannot make קידוש without wine (or bread), so the wine is the main thing. Reason 2 uses a general rule called תדיר קודם: a frequent מצוה or blessing goes before an infrequent one, and the wine blessing is said far more often than קידוש.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Another explanation.' It introduces a second reason.
Frequent / regular
The frequent thing comes first. This is a general rule for ordering מצוות and blessings.

steps.whyThisMatters: The rule תדיר קודם appears throughout ש"ס and is used to decide the order of many מצוות, for example which תפילה or which קרבן comes first.

phrases.english: And Beis Hillel say:
One blesses over the wine,
and afterward blesses over the day,
because the wine causes kiddush to be said.
phrases.notes: Without wine (or bread), there is no kiddush.

phrases.english: Another explanation:
the blessing over wine is frequent,
and the blessing over the day is not frequent.
When something frequent and something infrequent meet, the frequent one comes first.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים: מְבָרֵךְ עַל הַיַּיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the other side of the ברייתא's dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית הלל: bless the wine first, because the wine causes the קידוש and because תדיר קודם.

steps.title: The ברייתא rules like בית הלל
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends by ruling that the הלכה follows בית הלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is like the words of בית הלל.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא closes with a practical ruling: we follow בית הלל and bless the wine before the day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is why our קידוש starts with בורא פרי הגפן and only then says the blessing of the day. The גמרא will soon question why this line was needed at all (Step 10).

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law (Aramaic form of הֲלָכָה)

phrases.english: And the halacha is in accordance with the words of Beis Hillel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides the dispute presented in Steps 5–6.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In practice, the blessing on the wine comes before the blessing of the day.

steps.title: Why did בית הלל need a second reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the purpose is of בית הלל's 'דבר אחר', their extra second reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the purpose of 'another explanation'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why בית הלל added a second reason when their first reason already seemed good enough. The next step answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is not an attack on בית הלל. It is a question about the wording of the ברייתא: why bother adding a second reason at all?

keyTerms.meaning: What? / What is the point of?

phrases.english: What is the purpose of 'another explanation'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the second reason given in Step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why did בית הלל give a second reason?

steps.title: So בית הלל would also have two reasons, like בית שמאי
steps.stepSummary: Someone might think בית שמאי are stronger because they have two reasons and בית הלל only one. So בית הלל added a second reason: תדיר קודם.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you would say: there (בית שמאי) have two reasons and here (בית הלל) have only one, so בית שמאי should win. Here too there are two reasons: when something frequent and something infrequent meet, the frequent one comes first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the second reason was added so that בית הלל would not look weaker than בית שמאי, who gave two reasons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי's two reasons were 'the day causes the wine' and 'the day came first.' To match them, בית הלל added תדיר קודם to their 'the wine causes the קידוש.' Now the two sides are balanced, two reasons against two.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say (introduces a possible objection)
Two
One
Here too

phrases.english: And if you would say
there (Beis Shammai) there are two reasons, and here (Beis Hillel) only one,
phrases.notes: The point being: so בית שמאי would seem to have the stronger position.

phrases.english: here too there are two reasons:
when something frequent and something infrequent meet, the frequent one comes first.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא הָתָם תַּרְתֵּי וְהָכָא חֲדָא
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The second reason balances בית שמאי's two reasons, so no one would think בית שמאי's view is stronger.

steps.title: Why state the ruling? A בת קול already decided like בית הלל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ruling at the end of the ברייתא. A בת קול already announced that the הלכה always follows בית הלל, so why say it again here?
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And the הלכה is like בית הלל.' But that is obvious, since a בת קול came out and declared it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא's ruling again and challenges it as unnecessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בת קול (heavenly voice) famously declared that in general the הלכה follows בית הלל over בית שמאי. If so, there is no need to spell out the ruling in this specific case, so the line in the ברייתא seems pointless.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious! (a challenge that something did not need to be said)
A heavenly voice
Went out / emerged

phrases.english: 'And the halacha is like the words of Beis Hillel':
phrases.notes: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא's ruling from Step 7.

phrases.english: That is obvious,
since a heavenly voice already came out (declaring the halacha follows Beis Hillel)!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the ruling in Step 7 and challenges why it was needed.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling 'והילכתא כדברי בית הלל' in the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The בת קול already settled that the הלכה generally follows בית הלל, so stating it in this case adds nothing.

steps.title: First answer: this ברייתא was taught before the בת קול
steps.stepSummary: The first answer is that the ברייתא was taught before the בת קול came out, so back then the ruling still needed to be stated.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say: this was taught before the בת קול came out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its first answer: when this ברייתא was taught, the בת קול had not yet come out, so the ruling was new information.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling only looks obvious to us, who live after the בת קול. When the ברייתא was first said, nobody had yet been told to follow בית הלל in general. The words 'איבעית אימא' tell us that a second, alternative answer follows next.

keyTerms.meaning: If you wish, say. This introduces one possible answer, and usually another one follows.
Before

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up קוֹדֶם here ('before', in time) with קוֹדֵם in תדיר קודם ('takes precedence'). They look alike, but here it means the ברייתא was taught earlier in history than the בת קול.

phrases.english: If you wish, say:
this was taught before the heavenly voice,
phrases.notes: A second, alternative answer follows in the next step (step 12).

steps.terutzResolutionType: Historical timing: the source was taught before the general ruling existed.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ruling in the ברייתא seems pointless because the בת קול already decided like בית הלל.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא came before the בת קול, so at that time the ruling was needed.

steps.title: Second answer: the ruling follows רבי יהושע, who ignores a בת קול
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא could come from after the בת קול. It follows רבי יהושע, who says we do not decide הלכה based on a בת קול, so the ruling still had to be stated.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or, if you want, say that the ברייתא was taught after the בת קול. It follows רבי יהושע, who said that we do not pay attention to a בת קול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer to the question from step 10: why does the ברייתא say the הלכה follows בית הלל if a בת קול already announced it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first answer said the ברייתא came before the בת קול. This answer accepts that it came after, but says it follows רבי יהושע. In his view a בת קול cannot decide הלכה, so the ruling for בית הלל has to be stated on its own terms.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish, say: introduces another possible answer
A Heavenly Voice
We pay no attention to it
The תנא who famously said 'לא בשמים היא': Torah law is decided by people, not by Heaven

steps.whatToRemember: Two answers explain why the ruling for בית הלל is repeated. (1) The ברייתא was taught before the בת קול. (2) It was taught after the בת קול, but follows רבי יהושע, who ignores a בת קול.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying that רבי יהושע himself ruled on this dispute. It says that the ברייתא follows his approach, that a בת קול does not decide הלכה. So even after the בת קול, the ברייתא had to state on its own that the הלכה follows בית הלל.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
after the Heavenly Voice,
and it is the view of Rabbi Yehoshua,
who said: we pay no attention to a Heavenly Voice.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second, alternative answer to the same קשיא answered in step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the source to a specific תנא's view (רבי יהושע)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Once the בת קול spoke, there is no need to state the ruling again.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to רבי יהושע, a בת קול does not decide הלכה, so the ruling must be stated on its own.

steps.title: The first dipping of lettuce before the meal
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה begins. Vegetables are brought to the leader of the סדר, and he dips חזרת before reaching the bitter herbs eaten after the מצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: They brought vegetables before him. He dips the חזרת until he reaches the 'dessert of the bread', meaning the bitter herbs eaten after the מצה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts here. It describes the first dipping at the סדר, done with חזרת before the main part of the meal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If no other vegetable is on the table, he uses חזרת for this first dipping. 'פרפרת הפת' means the מרור eaten after the מצה. So this dipping comes before that stage.

keyTerms.meaning: Abbreviation for מַתְנִיתִין: our משנה
He dips
Lettuce, a type of bitter herb
The 'dessert' of the bread: the מרור eaten after the מצה

steps.confusionAlert: There are two dippings at the סדר. This line describes the first one, before the מצה. It is not the dipping of מרור later on.

phrases.english: MISHNA: They brought before him,
he dips the lettuce
before he reaches the dessert of the bread.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the next משנה, which continues the order of the סדר after the first cup described in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Before the meal, the leader dips חזרת as a first dipping, before reaching the מרור that comes after the מצה.

steps.title: The foods brought to the table, and the view that חרוסת is not a מצוה
steps.stepSummary: מצה, חזרת, חרוסת, and two cooked dishes are brought to the leader. The תנא קמא says חרוסת is not a מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They brought before him מצה, חזרת, חרוסת, and two cooked dishes, even though eating חרוסת is not a מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lists the main foods placed before the leader of the סדר. It notes that חרוסת is brought even though, in the first view, it is not a מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'even though' tells us חרוסת is only a custom according to the תנא קמא, yet it is still served. The two cooked dishes are brought in honor of the יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: A paste of fruits and nuts that the מרור is dipped into
Two cooked dishes
Even though

phrases.english: They brought before him matza
and lettuce and charoset
and two cooked dishes,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין חֲרוֹסֶת מִצְוָה.
phrases.english: even though charoset is not a מצוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה, moving from the first dipping to the main foods of the סדר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מצה, חזרת, חרוסת, and two cooked dishes are brought. According to the תנא קמא, חרוסת is not a מצוה.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר בן צדוק: חרוסת is a מצוה
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר בן צדוק disagrees and holds that חרוסת is a מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר בן צדוק says: חרוסת is a מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: A second תנא disagrees with the previous line about חרוסת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא sees חרוסת as only a custom. רבי אליעזר בן צדוק holds that eating it is an actual מצוה. The גמרא will later explain the reason for his view.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא who holds that חרוסת is a מצוה
A commandment, a real obligation

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer ben Tzadok says: it is a מצוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the תנא קמא's statement in step 14 that חרוסת is not a מצוה.

steps.title: When the בית המקדש stood, the קרבן פסח itself was brought
steps.stepSummary: When the בית המקדש stood, they also brought the body of the קרבן פסח to the leader.
steps.simpleTranslation: And in the בית המקדש era, they would bring the body of the קרבן פסח before him.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds what was served when the בית המקדש stood: the roasted קרבן פסח itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Today the סדר has מצה, מרור, and other foods. When the בית המקדש stood, the main food was the קרבן פסח, and it was placed in front of the leader together with everything else.

keyTerms.meaning: The Holy Temple
The body of the Paschal lamb, the קרבן פסח itself

steps.whyThisMatters: This line ties the סדר's foods back to the original קרבן פסח, which today we only remember (for example, through the זרוע on the plate).

phrases.english: And in the Temple they would bring before him
the body of the Paschal lamb.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the item served in the time of the בית המקדש to the list of foods in step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the בית המקדש stood, the קרבן פסח itself was brought before the leader of the סדר.
